title: Evacuation & Staggered Failover Capacity Sheet (GPU Fleet)
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet defines a staggered failover and controlled-evacuation approach for GPU fleets across regions. Goal is to size DR reserves and spare pools to support: (a) short-notice evacuation (network/region outage), (b) planned maintenance migrations, and (c) burst absorption during regional spikes while minimizing reserved cost.

Assumptions:
- Baseline production steady-state: 75% average utilization across all GPUs (based on Q4 2024 telemetry).
- Peak traffic distribution by region follows observed 95th-percentile request patterns (see linked artifacts).
- Failover priority groups: P0 (critical inference routes), P1 (low-latency product features), P2 (best-effort batch and async).
- Evacuation window targets: immediate (<30 min), short (30-180 min), planned (>3 hours).
- Reserve policy uses a probabilistic safety factor: reserve_factor = 1.20 for immediate, 1.10 for short, 1.05 for planned.

Live region capacity snapshot (snapshot date: 2025-02-10):
Region | Total GPUs | Prod Avg Util % | Prod 95th % Util (est) | Dedicated Spare Pool | Current DR Reserve GPUs | Evac Window Target | Primary Failover Targets
us-west1 | 480 | 72 | 95 | 48 | 60 | immediate | us-east4 (primary), eu-west1 (secondary)
us-east4 | 320 | 78 | 97 | 32 | 40 | short | us-west1 (primary), eu-west1 (secondary)
eu-west1 | 240 | 68 | 92 | 24 | 32 | short | us-east4 (primary), ap-southeast1 (secondary)
ap-southeast1 | 160 | 64 | 90 | 16 | 20 | planned | eu-west1 (primary), us-east4 (secondary)

Key calculations (per-region):
- Estimated peak demand GPUs = Total GPUs * (Prod 95th % Util / 100).
- Required immediate reserve = ceil(Estimated peak demand * (reserve_factor immediate) - Dedicated Spare Pool).
- If required immediate reserve > Current DR Reserve GPUs -> flag: "Top-up needed".

Example calculation for us-west1:
- Estimated peak demand GPUs = 480 * 0.95 = 456 GPUs
- Required immediate reserve = ceil(456 * 1.20 - 48) = ceil(547.2 - 48) = 500 GPUs -> Top-up needed (current DR reserve 60)
Note: Top-up numbers indicate we cannot meet full immediate failover with on-hand spare; plan is to use staggered failover (priority-based admission) to lower required headroom.

Staggered failover policy (proposal):
- Phase 0 (0-30m): Evacuate/route only P0 routes to primary failover; allocate cold-start buffer of 1.5x per-P0 baseline token throughput. Use pre-warmed spot instances where available.
- Phase 1 (30-180m): Bring P1 online with conservative concurrency caps (50% of normal concurrency) and spill to queued processing where possible. Start cross-region ephemeral scaling up to 10% of target region capacity using burst credit.
- Phase 2 (>3h): Gradually restore full capacity for P1 and P2, reapply autoscaling policies and scale down DR reserves if healthy.

Probability-driven reserve sizing (summary):
- Run Monte Carlo with historical outage frequency and region upstream dependency to estimate expected shortfall minutes. For conservative planning use 99th percentile shortfall.
- Translate shortfall minutes to GPU-minutes then to GPUs by dividing by evacuation window minutes.

Simulation scenarios (summary results):
1) short outage: us-west1 network partition for 45 minutes, traffic redistributed to us-east4 and eu-west1.
   - Without staggered policy: immediate shortfall = 120 GPUs -> high request drop for P1 routes.
   - With staggered policy: shortfall reduced to 28 GPUs, P0 preserved, P1 partially degraded.
2) regional data center maintenance (scheduled 6 hours): planned migration of 100 GPUs off us-east4 to ap-southeast1 over 4 hours.
   - Recommended: pre-warm 40 GPUs in ap-southeast1 2 hours before migration start; set concurrency cap for P1 at 60% during migration.
3) cascading region outage (us-east4 + eu-west1, 3 hours): worst-case stress test.
   - Required cross-region temporary capacity ~220 GPUs; recommend invoking emergency burst contracts with cloud partner and throttling non-critical batch jobs.

Operational playbook items (actionable):
- Maintain region DR reserve target as max(Current DR Reserve, calculated_required_shortfall) and reconcile monthly. Owner: Asha Kapoor.
- Implement priority routing flags in the router service to support P0/P1/P2 admission control. Owner: Liam Ortega.
- Add a scheduled job that computes real-time "evacuation readiness" metric every 5 minutes and surfaces it on the console. Owner: Maya Chen (SRE).
- Run a quarterly simulated evacuation drill (inject region blackout) and measure recovery time and user-impact metrics. Owner: SRE + Oncall.

Cost/benefit comments:
- Full immediate reserve to cover worst-case 95th*1.2 across all regions is cost-prohibitive (reserve blending leads to ~18% fleet overhead). Staggered failover with admit control reduces overhead to ~6-9% with acceptable P1 degradation windows.
- Consider hedging with short-term burst capacity contracts (reserve small baseline, buy burst credits for extreme events).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Validate the 95th-percentile utilization assumptions using the per-model telemetry (action: Research -> provide model-level 95th profiles).
- Legal: confirm SLA language for cross-region failover and customer-facing latency SLOs for P0 features.
- Finance: cost model for different reserve blend options (monthly reserved vs burst credits).

Appendix A: Quick reference checklist for an evacuation event:
- [ ] set router policy -> P0 only (Phase 0)
- [ ] scale up pre-warmed instances in primary failover region (+20% pre-warm) if available
- [ ] enable concurrency caps for P1
- [ ] notify customers affected by degraded P1 with templated message (link to template in linked_artifacts)
- [ ] kick off post-mortem and capacity accounting run after recovery

Appendix B: Short CSV snapshot (for quick import):
region,total_gpus,prod_avg_util,prod_95_util,spare_pool,current_dr_reserve,evac_window_mins
us-west1,480,72,95,48,60,30
us-east4,320,78,97,32,40,120
eu-west1,240,68,92,24,32,120
ap-southeast1,160,64,90,16,20,240

Notes: This is a working artifact. Numbers are intentionally conservative for planning. Do not treat "Required immediate reserve" as a procurement order until validated with model-level load tests.
